### workspace lock --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock <subcommand> [options]

Coordinates agents sharing a resource through one flock-guarded lock
store per repository. Locks are shared across every worktree of a
repository, keyed by its git common directory.

Subcommands:
  acquire       Take a lock, or wait in line for it
  release       Release a lock this agent holds
  status        Show who holds each lock and who is queued
  clear         Force-remove a lock's holder and queue
  instructions  Print the prompt block that tells a coding agent how to use a lock

Run `workspace lock VERB --help` for a verb's options and examples.
`lock clear` removes a holder and its waiters for real; for devenv it also
stops the dev env's process group.

Options (every subcommand):
  --name WS         Act on workspace WS instead of the one detected from the
                    current directory (the lock namespace is WS's repository)

Options (acquire):
  --task TEXT       Free-text description shown to other waiters
  --wait            Enqueue and poll instead of refusing when busy
  --poll DURATION   Time between polls while waiting, e.g. "5s" (a plain
                    number is seconds; default: 5)
  --max-wait DUR    Stop waiting after DUR, e.g. "9m" (a plain number is
                    seconds; exit 75; re-run to keep
                    waiting; implies --wait). This is when to give up
                    polling, not a hard deadline: if promoted to holder
                    at the instant DUR elapses, acquire still exits 0
                    holding the lock. Run `acquire --max-wait` in the
                    background and treat the process's exit code as
                    the signal, not the printed message.

Exit codes (acquire):
  0   acquired
  1   held by someone else (no --wait)
  3   this agent's hold was taken over while it was idle (see below);
      re-run to queue again
  4   cleared by someone else while waiting
  5   this agent already holds or waits for a different lock
      (release it first)
  75  still queued after --max-wait

Idle takeover: when a holding agent finishes its turn, the
session-event hook marks its lock idle; any prompt or tool use marks
it active again. Once idle for locks.idle_grace (default 5m; set with
`workspace config set locks.idle_grace 10m`), the first waiter in the
queue takes the lock over. The displaced agent is told once, on its
next acquire or release; acquire then carries on as usual, while
release exits 3. The dev environment lock is never taken over this way.

Workflow runs: a run can hold locks for a step. `status` shows such a
holder as `run <id> (step <name>)`. It is not tied to an agent's
session, is never idle and is never taken over; it is released when
the run moves on or ends. `acquire` from the pane bound to that run
reports the lock as already held for it (exit 0) instead of waiting.

Note: `lock release`/`lock clear` exit 0 even when nothing was
held/cleared, except that `release` exits 3 when it reports an idle
takeover, and `clear` exits 1 when it keeps the devenv lock because
the dev environment's process group could not be stopped (owned by
another user, or still running after SIGKILL), or because it is
already being cleared by another `lock clear` (check the result with
`workspace lock status <name>`). `acquire` has its own exit codes above.

Enforcement: once hooks are installed (see `workspace init`/`doctor`),
Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit are denied (exit 2) for any agent
that isn't the edit lock's holder. Bash-based edits (sed, git apply,
codegen) aren't covered and stay advisory. The edit lock is released
automatically on SessionEnd and on a `/clear`'d SessionStart.

Examples:
  workspace lock acquire edit    # take the edit lock, or exit 1 with an error if another agent holds it
  workspace lock acquire edit --wait --task "PROJ-12 fix login"    # queue for the edit lock; blocks, so run it in the background
  workspace lock acquire edit --max-wait 9m    # queue, but give up after 9 minutes with exit 75
  workspace lock release edit   # give the edit lock back when the edits are done
  workspace lock status    # every lock of this repository, with its holder and queue
  workspace lock status edit --json    # the edit lock as JSON, for a script
  workspace lock clear edit    # person only: remove a lost holder and its waiters for real
  workspace lock instructions edit    # the prompt block to paste into an agent's instructions
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace lock acquire --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock acquire NAME [--name WS] [--task TEXT] [--wait] [--poll DURATION] [--max-wait DURATION]

Take a lock, or wait in line for it.

Takes lock NAME for the calling coding agent, for real. NAME is any label you choose; `edit` is the one
the edit-guard hook enforces, denying other agents' Edit and Write calls while it is held. The hold
lasts until `lock release`, the agent's SessionEnd or the agent process dying. Run it inside an agent's session, which names the holder: from a
plain shell it exits 1 with an error. Locks are shared by every worktree of a repository.

Without --wait a busy lock exits 1 with an error. With --wait (or --max-wait) it queues and polls until it
is promoted, which can take a long time: run it in the background and read its exit code, not its text.
--max-wait is when to stop polling, not a hard deadline: a promotion at that instant still exits 0.
A holder idle for locks.idle_grace (default 5m) is taken over by the first waiter.

Exit codes:
  0   acquired
  1   held by someone else (no --wait), or the agent could not be identified
  4   cleared by someone else while waiting
  5   this agent already holds or waits for a different lock (release it first)
  75  gave up after --max-wait; no longer queued, run it again to queue
  130 interrupted by SIGINT while waiting; the wait is withdrawn
  143 interrupted by SIGTERM while waiting; the wait is withdrawn

Options:
    --name NAME                  Act on this workspace's repository instead of the one detected from the current directory
    --task TEXT                  Free-text description shown to other waiters
    --wait                       Queue and poll instead of exiting 1 when busy
    --poll DURATION              Time between polls while waiting, e.g. "5s" (a plain number is seconds; default: 5)
    --max-wait DURATION          Stop waiting after DURATION, e.g. "9m" (a plain number is seconds); exits 75; implies --wait
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace lock acquire edit    # take the edit lock, or exit 1 with an error if another agent holds it
  workspace lock acquire edit --wait --task "PROJ-12 fix login"    # queue behind the holder and show the task to waiters; blocks, so run it in the background
  workspace lock acquire edit --max-wait 9m    # queue, but give up after 9 minutes with exit 75 (no longer queued; run it again to queue)
  workspace lock acquire edit --wait --poll 10s    # check the queue every 10 seconds instead of every 5
  workspace lock acquire edit --name api-fix    # take the lock of the repository that workspace api-fix belongs to
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace lock release --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock release [NAME | --all] [--name WS] [--json]

Release a lock this agent holds.

Gives the lock back, for real, so the first waiter is promoted. Like acquire it runs inside an agent's
session. A lock this agent does not hold is a message and exit 0; release exits 3 when it reports that
this agent's hold was taken over while it was idle. Give NAME or --all, not both.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Act on this workspace's repository instead of the one detected from the current directory
    --all                        Release every lock this agent holds
    --json                       Print one action document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes to stderr
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace lock release edit    # give the edit lock back when the edits are done
  workspace lock release --all    # give back every lock this agent holds
  workspace lock release edit --name api-fix    # release in the repository that workspace api-fix belongs to
  workspace lock release edit --json    # one action document on stdout, for a script
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace lock status --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock status [NAME] [--name WS] [--json]

Show who holds each lock and who is queued.

Read-only: it changes nothing and needs no agent session. A holder whose process is gone is marked
STALE, an idle one IDLE. Every lock of the repository is listed without NAME. Locks are also logged in
locks.jsonl next to locks.json (see docs/README.lock.md).

Options:
    --name NAME                  Act on this workspace's repository instead of the one detected from the current directory
    --json                       Print the documented JSON (see docs/README.lock.md) instead of text
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace lock status    # every lock of this repository, with its holder and queue
  workspace lock status edit    # only the edit lock; "edit lock is free" when no one holds it
  workspace lock status --json    # holders and queues as JSON, for a script
  workspace lock status edit --name api-fix    # the edit lock of the repository that workspace api-fix belongs to
--- stderr
--- end

Locks are also logged in\nlocks.jsonl next to locks.json (see docs/README.lock.md).","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Act on this workspace's repository instead of the one detected from the current directory"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print the documented JSON (see docs/README.lock.md) instead of text"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace lock status","scenario":"every lock of this repository, with its holder and queue"},{"command":"workspace lock status edit","scenario":"only the edit lock; \"edit lock is free\" when no one holds it"},{"command":"workspace lock status --json","scenario":"holders and queues as JSON, for a script"},{"command":"workspace lock status edit --name api-fix","scenario":"the edit lock of the repository that workspace api-fix belongs to"}]}

### workspace lock clear --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock clear [NAME | --all] [--name WS] [--json]

Force-remove a lock's holder and queue.

Meant for the person: it removes the holder and every waiter for real, so an agent that holds the lock
loses it. Agents release their own lock instead.

For devenv it also stops the dev environment's process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after
dev.stop_timeout) and keeps the lock until that group is stopped. Ordinary waiters are removed once the
lock is cleared, but stay queued if a kept devenv holder cannot be stopped; a queued `dev up --force` is
kept either way.

Exits 0 even when nothing was held. Exits 1 when it keeps the devenv lock because the process group
could not be stopped (owned by another user, or still running after SIGKILL) or because another
`lock clear` is already stopping it; check with `workspace lock status NAME`.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Act on this workspace's repository instead of the one detected from the current directory
    --all                        Clear every lock in this repository
    --json                       Print the documented JSON (see docs/README.lock.md) instead of text
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace lock clear edit    # free the edit lock after its holder was lost; its waiters are removed
  workspace lock clear devenv    # stop the dev environment's processes and free the devenv lock (`dev down` is the normal way)
  workspace lock clear --all    # reset every lock in this repository
  workspace lock clear edit --json    # the result of the clear as JSON, for a script
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace lock instructions --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock instructions [NAME]

Print the prompt block that tells a coding agent how to use a lock.

Prints text and nothing else, for pasting into an agent's instructions. NAME defaults to edit. The block
tells the agent to acquire the lock in the background with --wait, wait for "Acquired", and release it
when its edits are done.

Options:
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace lock instructions    # the block for the edit lock, to paste into an agent's instructions
  workspace lock instructions edit | pbcopy    # copy the edit lock's block to the clipboard
  workspace lock instructions migrations    # the same block for a lock named migrations
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace lock
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace lock <subcommand> [options]

Coordinates agents sharing a resource through one flock-guarded lock
store per repository. Locks are shared across every worktree of a
repository, keyed by its git common directory.

Subcommands:
  acquire       Take a lock, or wait in line for it
  release       Release a lock this agent holds
  status        Show who holds each lock and who is queued
  clear         Force-remove a lock's holder and queue
  instructions  Print the prompt block that tells a coding agent how to use a lock

Run `workspace lock VERB --help` for a verb's options and examples.
`lock clear` removes a holder and its waiters for real; for devenv it also
stops the dev env's process group.

Options (every subcommand):
  --name WS         Act on workspace WS instead of the one detected from the
                    current directory (the lock namespace is WS's repository)

Options (acquire):
  --task TEXT       Free-text description shown to other waiters
  --wait            Enqueue and poll instead of refusing when busy
  --poll DURATION   Time between polls while waiting, e.g. "5s" (a plain
                    number is seconds; default: 5)
  --max-wait DUR    Stop waiting after DUR, e.g. "9m" (a plain number is
                    seconds; exit 75; re-run to keep
                    waiting; implies --wait). This is when to give up
                    polling, not a hard deadline: if promoted to holder
                    at the instant DUR elapses, acquire still exits 0
                    holding the lock. Run `acquire --max-wait` in the
                    background and treat the process's exit code as
                    the signal, not the printed message.

Exit codes (acquire):
  0   acquired
  1   held by someone else (no --wait)
  3   this agent's hold was taken over while it was idle (see below);
      re-run to queue again
  4   cleared by someone else while waiting
  5   this agent already holds or waits for a different lock
      (release it first)
  75  still queued after --max-wait

Idle takeover: when a holding agent finishes its turn, the
session-event hook marks its lock idle; any prompt or tool use marks
it active again. Once idle for locks.idle_grace (default 5m; set with
`workspace config set locks.idle_grace 10m`), the first waiter in the
queue takes the lock over. The displaced agent is told once, on its
next acquire or release; acquire then carries on as usual, while
release exits 3. The dev environment lock is never taken over this way.

Workflow runs: a run can hold locks for a step. `status` shows such a
holder as `run <id> (step <name>)`. It is not tied to an agent's
session, is never idle and is never taken over; it is released when
the run moves on or ends. `acquire` from the pane bound to that run
reports the lock as already held for it (exit 0) instead of waiting.

Note: `lock release`/`lock clear` exit 0 even when nothing was
held/cleared, except that `release` exits 3 when it reports an idle
takeover, and `clear` exits 1 when it keeps the devenv lock because
the dev environment's process group could not be stopped (owned by
another user, or still running after SIGKILL), or because it is
already being cleared by another `lock clear` (check the result with
`workspace lock status <name>`). `acquire` has its own exit codes above.

Enforcement: once hooks are installed (see `workspace init`/`doctor`),
Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit are denied (exit 2) for any agent
that isn't the edit lock's holder. Bash-based edits (sed, git apply,
codegen) aren't covered and stay advisory. The edit lock is released
automatically on SessionEnd and on a `/clear`'d SessionStart.

Examples:
  workspace lock acquire edit    # take the edit lock, or exit 1 with an error if another agent holds it
  workspace lock acquire edit --wait --task "PROJ-12 fix login"    # queue for the edit lock; blocks, so run it in the background
  workspace lock acquire edit --max-wait 9m    # queue, but give up after 9 minutes with exit 75
  workspace lock release edit   # give the edit lock back when the edits are done
  workspace lock status    # every lock of this repository, with its holder and queue
  workspace lock status edit --json    # the edit lock as JSON, for a script
  workspace lock clear edit    # person only: remove a lost holder and its waiters for real
  workspace lock instructions edit    # the prompt block to paste into an agent's instructions
--- stderr
--- end
